name: Ukiyo-e
garments: not a fashion look — a woodblock print tradition, though it depicts kimono fashion of its era extensively

media.title: Katsushika Hokusai, The Great Wave off Kanagawa (c. 1831)
Utagawa Hiroshige, 100 Famous Views of Edo (1856–58)

reacts_against: no single Western movement; it developed independently as popular, affordable urban art ("pictures of the floating world") for merchant-class buyers excluded from elite painting patronage.
revivals: directly cited by Impressionist and Post-Impressionist painters (Van Gogh collected and copied ukiyo-e prints) after Japan reopened to trade in the 1850s-60s, a cross-cultural influence historians call Japonisme

wiki_facts.key_motifs: Courtesans and beautiful women (bijin-ga), kabuki actors (yakusha-e), landscapes (fūkei-ga), scenes from history and folklore, sumo wrestlers, nature scenes
wiki_facts.key_colours: Rich and varied palettes, often with bold black outlines and flat areas of color
wiki_facts.key_values: Appreciation of transient pleasures, urban entertainment culture, beauty, theatricality, observation of nature and daily life

findings: light — about 43% of the measured color is pale or near-white
mostly muted — about 68% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from the Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
